structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the equiangular-spiral angle alpha = arctan(2π/ln W), computed from measured per-whorl expansion rate W of typical spiral gastropod shells, is almost never below 80° (W>3.0) and its bulk lies between 80° and 85° (W≈1.73–3.0).
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using the gastropod specimens with a valid whorl expansion rate, convert W per full revolution to alpha = arctan(2π/ln W). PASS if (a) at least 90% of specimens have alpha >= 80° (i.e. 'very seldom less than 80°') AND (b) at least 50% of specimens have alpha in [80°, 85°] (i.e. 'usually between'), with the sample median in [80°, 85°].
structured_output.fail_criterion: FAIL if more than 20% of specimens have alpha < 80° (W>3.0), or fewer than 50% fall in [80°, 85°], or the median lies outside [80°, 85°]. Results between the pass and fail thresholds (10–20% below 80°) are inconclusive.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'constant angle' is the angle between the tangent and the radius vector of an equiangular spiral; it relates to the whorl expansion per turn as tan(alpha) = 2π/ln W, so W=3 gives about 80° (his Nautilus figure) and 85° corresponds to W≈1.73. The dataset's whorl expansion rate must be expressed per full revolution (convert if given per radian or per whorl fraction). Modern reinterpretation: Collins et al. fit a helicospiral (the spire also translates along the axis), so the planar expansion rate is the analogue of Thompson's spiral and alpha is a derived quantity, not measured directly. The dataset covers only gastropods (176 fossil and living shells), so it tests only the gastropod part of the claim; the nautiloid and ammonitoid parts (including Nautilus at about 80° and W≈3) cannot be decided by this dataset and need a separate test. 'Typically spiral' is approximated by all helicospiral species in the sample.

dataset.name: Data associated with: Going round the twist – An empirical analysis of shell coiling in helicospiral gastropods
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data from Collins et al., Paleobiology)
dataset.why_it_fits: It gives measured coiling parameters for 176 fossil and living helicospiral gastropod shells, including whorl expansion rate. The file S_Table_3_hangle_output.csv (hangle output) and S_Table_1_Specimens.csv plus S_Table_2_metadata.csv (specimen identity and taxonomy) allow per-specimen conversion of the expansion rate to Thompson's constant angle. The column names are not described on the landing page, so they must be checked in the CSVs and the .Rmd scripts. It covers gastropods only, not nautiloids or ammonoids.
